evidence.exact_quote: The following canonical documents govern this spec. This document MUST NOT redefine schemas or contracts owned by those sources; it adds the IDE UX layer on top of them.

items.impact: Prevents GitHub Integration from forking auth, storage, command, and secret-handling contracts.
items.statement: The prologue locks the GitHub API-only/auth realm, OS credential-store, local-git, remote-SSH, UICommand, and imported-SSOT boundaries; these are explicit non-discretionary constraints.
items.title: Locked SSOT and secret boundary

evidence.exact_quote: `Plans/GitHub_Integration.md` remains the owner doc for Source Control and GitHub Actions user-facing integration, hosted workflow/admin/runtime surfaces, Source Control worktree UI, GitHub route/open propagation, remote GitHub transport disclosure, and GitHub consumer safety carry-through. Cross-doc consumers must preserve the owner boundaries in the source body and ContractRefs rather than recreating GitHub-local auth, status, storage, FileSafe, model, or command contracts.

items.impact: Provides an explicit owner/consumer split and forbids local redefinition of imported runtime contracts.
items.statement: The continuation explicitly owns the user-facing Source Control and Actions surfaces while consuming auth, runtime-status, storage, FileSafe, model, route/open, approval, and remote-search authorities.
items.title: Owner and consumer reconciliation

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: GitHub Integration preserves canonical owner-section requirements, stable account identity, SSOT references, anti-drift compliance, github_api realm separation, no-secret storage, local git and SSH subprocess decisions, and UICommand dispatch boundaries while refusing to redefine contracts owned by GitHub API auth, Contracts, storage, or UI command catalogs.

canonical_text: 'GitHub Integration separates Source Control, GitHub Actions, GitHub Copilot, and GitHub API: Source Control owns Git-first repo/worktree GUI behavior, GitHub Actions owns hosted workflow/admin/runtime GUI behavior, GitHub API remains internal plumbing, and legacy Git (GitHub) labels cannot collapse hosted behavior into Source Control.'

canonical_text: Source Control exposes Changes, History, Graph, Worktrees, Branches/Stash, diff preview, staging, commit, sync, stash, branch, incoming/outgoing, conflict, and multi-SCM provider behavior; accordion headers are accessible buttons and compare defaults are deterministic by origin.

items.impact: Locks the primary surface separation, interaction catalog, accessibility role, and compare-origin defaults.
items.statement: GI-002 through GI-004 define a coherent non-secret SSOT boundary and separate Git-first Source Control from hosted GitHub Actions, with deterministic compare defaults and accessible accordion controls.
items.title: Source Control and Actions surface contract

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: GitHub compare/open pivots carry closed compare_origin identity, project/repo/worktree/run refs, account scoping, multi-lane context, and active repo/worktree/run binding instead of reconstructing targets from local UI state or flattening multiple contexts into a single branch.

canonical_text: GitHub auth, admin, readiness, history, Source Control, Actions subviews, run history, compare/review, and recovery surfaces disclose requested and effective execution identity by consuming runtime identity fields and storing only resource, capability, readiness, and route/open refs needed for the same audit snapshot.

items.impact: Prevents cross-repo, cross-worktree, and cross-account target substitution during compare, review, and recovery.
items.statement: GI-005 and GI-006 require canonical compare-origin identity plus requested/effective account disclosure rather than reconstruction from mutable UI state.
items.title: Compare and account identity binding

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Search routing preserves focused_run_id, safe-point retry opens an explicit restore/retry confirmation with repo, worktree, branch, baseline/head, safe_point_id, affected files, owner run/node/attempt, and follow-up action, and run-aware compare-origin forwarding preserves identity and refs into review/conflict/safe-point contexts.

items.impact: Avoids silent focus changes and destructive retry against an unvalidated worktree or baseline.
items.statement: GI-007 specifies focus preservation and an explicit, identity-rich safe-point restore/retry confirmation, including a no-change outcome when declined.
items.title: Focus-safe restore and retry

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: GitHub Actions has Current Branch, Workflows, and Settings as stable subviews, routes compatibility entrypoints to the correct owner surface, and owns only GitHub-specific Settings, readiness, workflow, admin, and source-control ConfigKey schema details while importing shared storage rules.

canonical_text: Pinned critical workflows are owned by GitHub Actions > Workflows, use canonical pin/unpin commands and compatibility aliases, store workflow/repo/branch/worktree/badge/preference/provenance records, and expose stale or renamed workflow state without hiding historical receipts.

canonical_text: Replay from last known good belongs to GitHub Actions failure triage/history, compares failed runs against same-workflow same-branch successes, records baseline and comparison metadata, exposes compare options, and never implies rerun tests latest branch head unless a new dispatch occurs.

items.impact: Maintains hosted-surface ownership, durable pin provenance, and truthful last-known-good replay semantics.
items.statement: GI-008 through GI-010 establish the Actions information architecture, pinned-workflow lifecycle, and same-branch replay semantics with compatibility routing that cannot change ownership.
items.title: Actions IA, pins, and replay

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Current Branch shows active branch/worktree binding, background run status, Actions readiness, admin/runtime scopes, rate-limit/repo linkage, capability, environment-gated wait/blocked states, and recovery CTAs while live GitHub Actions Settings remains source of truth for hosted admin state.

canonical_text: Actions readiness is event-driven plus bounded refresh on project, branch/worktree, workflow-file, panel, dispatch-form, and admin CRUD events; stale readiness cannot authorize mutation, dispatchability is validated without persisting secrets, and capability disclosure shows scope/value limits honestly.

items.impact: Prevents stale readiness or template defaults from authorizing hosted mutation and keeps background context visible without stealing focus.
items.statement: GI-011 and GI-012 define live-admin precedence, event-driven readiness refresh, stale-state mutation denial, and explicit capability limits.
items.title: Readiness lifecycle and mutation gate

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Actions-to-code correlation links runs, jobs, steps, failed checks, command pivots, commit ranges, changed files, branch/worktree refs, and related diffs/worktrees as a remediation bridge while labeling heuristic uncertainty and preserving candidate choices.

canonical_text: Run impact mapping belongs to GitHub Actions run detail and Orchestrator receipts, shows branch/commit/PR, worktree, deploy chain, publish, and readiness implications, and marks incomplete evidence as partial rather than complete truth.

items.impact: Different implementations can choose incompatible confidence thresholds, candidate ordering, retention bounds, and large-monorepo behavior while still satisfying the prose.
items.statement: GI-013 and GI-014 correctly label heuristic and partial evidence, but do not define the confidence threshold value, deterministic candidate tie-break, impact-map retention limits, pagination/cardinality limits, or executable false-positive and false-negative oracles.
items.title: Correlation and impact-map algorithms remain discretionary

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Failure triage view compresses failed runs into failing job/step, logs, changed files, likely next action, metadata, log access/fallback state, tiered fetching, and stored refs while GitHub Actions repro loops follow Debug investigation budget reset rules.

canonical_text: Workflow authoring assistance is a GitHub Actions Settings/workflow-editor capability with language-service validation, completion, docs, remote-repo disclosure, proxy mediation, generation links, and preview/apply behavior that stores metadata only before accepted edits.

items.impact: Builders must invent log truncation thresholds, fetch-tier sizes, proxy failure behavior, apply atomicity, and rollback outcomes.
items.statement: GI-015 and GI-016 define failure-triage and authoring boundaries, but leave quantitative log tiers, truncation/download integrity, proxy retry semantics, preview-to-apply concurrency, partial-write handling, and rollback acceptance tests unspecified.
items.title: Failure triage and workflow apply need executable boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Actions readiness blocked-state taxonomy uses canonical actions_* reason details layered onto shared blocked metadata, maps auth expiration to shared failure class, exposes ordered allowed actions and active repo/branch context, and keeps attention_required distinct from blocked.

canonical_text: Hosted Git governance blockers use policy-specific reasons and receipts for protected branch, force-push, required PR/merge queue/status/signed commit/tag, actor bypass, lifecycle, fallback, and mutation outcome instead of generic branch-rule mismatch.

items.impact: Enables deterministic UI recovery and audit receipts for distinct hosted policy denials.
items.statement: GI-017 and GI-018 preserve distinct attention, blocked, auth, policy, and fallback states rather than collapsing them into generic failure.
items.title: Blocked and governance state taxonomy

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Source Control remains worktree-native with compare/lineage/recovery pivots, topology ownership over branch lineage, ownership badges, worktree safety warnings, run lifecycle claims/releases, restart recovery unknown ownership, and strong-action confirmations.

canonical_text: Worktrees rows are first-class Source Control objects with narrow-pane single-column expandable rows, row labels, actions, per-project All/Threads/Orchestrator/Manual filter persistence, and two-level accordion scroll behavior.

canonical_text: Hosted-repo, remote, and workflow lifecycle states are first-class, archived/deleted/historical-only states disable mutation deterministically, receipts retain immutable identifiers and refs, deep links reopen only through safe validated refs, and capability disclosure separates hosted-only mutation boundaries from local editing.

items.impact: Large repositories and keyboard-only users could receive inconsistent virtualization, focus, scroll, and destructive-confirmation behavior.
items.statement: GI-019 through GI-021 give strong lifecycle and destructive-action semantics, but do not set topology size limits, virtualization/loading behavior, keyboard navigation and focus order for expandable rows, or deterministic handling of concurrent ownership changes during confirmation.
items.title: Worktree UI is semantically strong but operationally incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: GitHub Integration consumes runtime status, bridge classification, tool dispatch, FileSafe, and storage startup contracts via explicit cross-ref anchors, displays canonical runtime outcomes, and treats legacy stop.* wording only as stale or compatibility input when it conflicts with kill.* and done.* families.

canonical_text: Hosted mutation dispatch, rerun, cancel, admin mutation, and Source Control hosted actions respect Tools listener, OAuth/listener failure semantics, FileSafe path checks, storage logical roots/startup locks/read-only degradation, and usage/cost display rules owned by FinalGUISpec.

canonical_text: GitHub Integration consumes route_target and OpenSubject semantics, resolves github:// resources and concerns into active routes and orchestrator concern records, preserves stable object identity for /jump/search-result routes, and treats Orchestrator references as supersession pointers rather than override evidence.

items.impact: Prevents local status forks, unsafe mutation during degraded startup, and identity loss across GitHub route/open pivots.
items.statement: GI-022 through GI-024 consistently consume canonical runtime/status, mutation-gate, usage-display, and object-routing contracts.
items.title: Runtime, mutation, and routing seams

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Graph patch flows use explicit graph_patch_request and graph_patch_result records carrying patch point, concern refs, structural change summary, affected generation, and requester identity before GitHub Integration exposes review or apply actions.

canonical_text: GitHub workflow approval and observation consumers preserve approval_scope, approval_id, PR review ID, execution_unit_id, compatibility HITL/tier-boundary inputs, blocked runtime overlays, and wait/timeout timestamps while scheduled workflows remain stale or unknown until concrete hosted observation exists.

items.impact: A stale or duplicate graph-patch apply can race approval or generation changes without a defined rejection, idempotency, compensating action, or recovery receipt.
items.statement: GI-025 and GI-026 bind graph patches and approvals to identities, generations, and observations, but do not define apply authority, optimistic-concurrency preconditions, idempotency keys, duplicate delivery handling, partial-apply rollback, cancellation races, or executable transition oracles.
items.title: Graph patch and approval concurrency is unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: GitHub remote, SSH, Actions, and repository operations carry FileSafe, permission, credential, redaction, projection-trust, hard_gate, remote path guard, SSH keepalive/reconnect, and storage-owned remote-search authority instead of bypassing gates or defining alternate remote search behavior locally.

canonical_text: Remote Git/non-Git search acceleration is remote-admin/user-visible transport; GitHub Integration owns remote cache/admin disclosure, consumes storage-owned staging/verification/re-anchor/remote-admin contracts, and keeps no-silent-local-fallback mandatory.

items.impact: Symlink, case-folding, TOCTOU, reconnect-during-write, and partially verified cache cases can produce security or truth-substitution failures if delegated contracts do not supply exact tests.
items.statement: GI-027 and GI-028 establish the correct security and no-local-fallback boundary, but this document does not bind canonicalization to symlink resolution and case rules, define TOCTOU resistance, specify in-flight mutation fate on disconnect, or provide adversarial remote-cache verification oracles.
items.title: Remote path and reconnect edge cases remain open

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Remote tool/provider execution uses GitHub remote context, remote SSH/reconnect budget, path guard, and storage verification anchors before mutating or reporting search/cache state.

items.impact: Remote disconnect or verification-anchor change during a mutation has no locally stated commit, abort, quarantine, or retry contract.
items.statement: GI-029 correctly gates remote mutation on context, reconnect budget, path guard, and verification anchors, but leaves the atomicity and stale-anchor behavior of in-flight remote tool mutations discretionary.
items.title: Remote execution transaction semantics

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: GitHub Integration consumes GitHub_AuthContext, includes effective_account_id in API calls, uses runtime identity resolution for cross-account capability checks, and follows scoped provider/model settings tied to Persona and execution_unit_type rather than repository or organization.

items.impact: A capability or account change between check and API dispatch can make the audit identity stale or authorize the wrong account.
items.statement: GI-030 defines effective-account attribution and cross-account checks, but not token/account snapshot freshness, check-to-use race handling, per-request revalidation, audit behavior for failed preflight, or retention/redaction rules for account identity in receipts.
items.title: Effective-account check has a TOCTOU seam

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The former GitHub_Integration doc-level source-preserving bridge is retired after Phase 2B atomized GitHub_Integration-S0002, S0004, S0006, and S0008 through S0012 into GI-002 through GI-030 and structurally dispositioned S0001, S0003, S0005, S0007, S0013, S0014, and S0016. GI-001 remains only as migration lineage for GitHub_Integration-S0015 and must not re-own atomized source coverage or use source_preserving_planunit compile mode.

items.impact: Prevents retired migration lineage from regaining product authority or generating executable work.
items.statement: GI-001 is explicitly retired to lineage-only status and cannot re-own atomized product coverage or use the retired source-preserving compile mode.
items.title: Retired bridge is unambiguous

evidence.exact_quote: GitHub optional promotion records PR and GitHub Actions evidence only when configured.
- Do not block local-only planning or build completion solely because GitHub is unavailable.
- GitHub Integration does not become the discovery behavior, search, or ranking owner.

items.impact: Promotion, repository attachment, and remote discovery span several owners without a complete failure matrix or a single typed receipt/handoff contract in this owner doc.
items.statement: GI-031 through GI-033 preserve GitHub-optional local truth and discovery ownership, but do not fully define caller initiation, cancellation and retry ownership, partial push/PR/check outcomes, duplicate promotion requests, repository-attachment rollback, or typed cross-owner receipt reconciliation.
items.title: Optional promotion and discovery handoffs need closure

evidence.exact_quote: github_update_workflow (P1) is compiled as canonical Puppet Master intent for github_update_workflow: Add GitHubUpdateCurrentness and ReleaseTagVerifier The preserved PM gap/delta is: Need rate-limit-safe updater and release/action tag currentness guard The observed external-repo signal remains source-lineage evidence: OpenCode upgrade GitHub API 403 and stale github@latest action issues

items.impact: The P1 supply-chain control can be implemented with incompatible endpoints, cache rules, rate-limit behavior, version semantics, and rollback policy, including unsafe failure-open behavior.
items.statement: GI-034 names GitHubUpdateCurrentness and ReleaseTagVerifier but does not define their inputs/outputs, caller and consumer, persisted state, authenticated-versus-unauthenticated selection, conditional request/cache behavior, rate-limit budget and backoff, release/tag comparison semantics, concurrency, offline posture, or recovery/rollback states.
items.title: GitHub update workflow lacks an implementable contract

evidence.exact_quote: - Unauthenticated/authenticated API fallback tests
- stale tag detection

items.impact: Passing tests can exercise different cases and expected outcomes, so the plan cannot certify rate-limit safety or release/action tag currentness consistently.
items.statement: GI-034 acceptance criteria are labels rather than executable oracles: they omit fixtures, endpoint/status matrices, Retry-After and reset handling, version/tag ordering rules, stale/current/unknown expected states, failure-open versus failure-closed policy, and receipt assertions.
items.title: GI-034 acceptance criteria are not test-complete

segments.summary: Reviewed the complete prologue for locked GitHub, auth, secret, local-git, remote-SSH, UICommand, SSOT, surface, identity, readiness, worktree, lifecycle, runtime-status, route/open, approval, and security constraints.
Reviewed owner reconciliation and GI-002 through GI-007 for SSOT, surface ownership, accessibility, compare identity, requested/effective identity, focus preservation, and safe-point recovery.

Reviewed GI-008 through GI-014 for Actions IA, pins, replay, readiness, live-admin precedence, dispatch capability, actions-to-code correlation, and impact mapping; quantitative heuristic and scale oracles remain incomplete.

Reviewed GI-015 through GI-021 for triage, authoring, blocked and governance taxonomies, worktree ownership/layout, destructive actions, and hosted lifecycle; operational, accessibility, and concurrency oracles are incomplete.

Reviewed GI-022 through GI-028 for runtime/status imports, mutation gates, object routing, graph patches, approvals, observation freshness, remote path security, reconnect, and no-local-fallback; concurrency and adversarial recovery contracts remain underspecified.

Reviewed GI-029, GI-030, retired GI-001, and GI-031 through GI-033 for remote execution, effective account identity, migration retirement, optional promotion, repository attachment, and remote discovery handoffs.

Reviewed GI-034 and the following concrete FABLE addendum lines. The update-currentness and release-tag intent remains non-implementable and its acceptance labels remain non-falsifiable despite adjacent Actions transport and reason-table detail.
